clue.text: Variations may be broadcast

parts.note: musical variations are written on a tune or air, and the phrase for that position also means being transmitted by radio or television

explanation.surface: A remark that a set of musical variations might get a radio airing.
explanation.walkthrough: Variations are composed 'on' a theme or air, so the whole clue plays on the stock phrase for being transmitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being transmitted live by radio or television is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Composer is beheaded

indicators.note: to behead a word is to cut off its first letter, here the one at the front of the synonym

parts.note: to be is to exist, so 'is' can mean lives

explanation.surface: A grim announcement that some composer has been executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word but is the fodder: it means LIVES (exists), and 'beheaded' drops its first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American composer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Voice of a cat that swallowed its tail?

indicators.note: swallowing its tail means the final letter of the animal's name is taken back inside the word

parts.note: a civet is a catlike mammal, often called a civet cat

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what a cat that ate its own tail would sound like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' tempts a feline word, but it is a civet; 'that swallowed its tail' moves its last letter inside, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the active is one of the two voices of a verb, alongside the passive.

clue.text: Composer's first little room that's right for a keyboard

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a small room
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A composer's first small music room comes fitted with the right keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument, or the keyboard itself, as in Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier.

clue.text: Tense under strain and impermeable

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: a strain is a tune, as is an air
tight means tense, as a stretched rope is

explanation.surface: Someone stressed and under pressure, closed off from everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress but means a tune, AIR; 'under' puts TIGHT below it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impermeable lets nothing through, the sense of sealed against air.

clue.text: Reproducer of Trojan holding note at a pub

indicators.note: holding means the hero's name contains the musical note inside it

parts.note: Hector was the Trojan prince and champion in the Iliad
G is one of the notes of the scale
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A Trojan clutching a musical note at a pub copies things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. A hectograph was an early copying device using a gelatine pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectograph made many copies of a document from a gelatine master, so it reproduces.

clue.text: Fellow in love entering ancient civilisation

indicators.note: entering means the following pieces go inside the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A man falls in love and joins an ancient culture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoan civilisation of Bronze Age Crete is named after the legendary King Minos.

clue.text: Composer of Lucia von -, which can't be mistaken

indicators.note: one who composes puts letters together in a new order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to name the composer of an opera about Lucia von Somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash tempts you to fill in a surname, but 'Composer of' asks you to rearrange LUCIA VON.
explanation.definitionFit: Univocal means having only one possible meaning, so it is unambiguous.

clue.text: Boadicea's part in the Celtic enigma

indicators.note: in signals the answer is concealed within the next two words

explanation.surface: The question of Boadicea's role in some Celtic mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Boadicea, or Boudicca, led the Iceni, the British tribe she belonged to and ruled.

clue.text: Holy smoke, as demonstrated

definitions.meaning: an old word for frankincense, the resin burned as incense in church
in this way, as has just been shown

explanation.definitionFit: Thus is both an archaic name for frankincense and the adverb meaning in this manner.

clue.text: "Come Dancing" with Carl Maria von -

definitions.meaning: a literal request to join the dance, and also a BBC ballroom programme
Carl Maria von Weber wrote a famous piano rondo of this title

explanation.walkthrough: Come Dancing was a long-running British TV ballroom show; the dash leaves Weber's surname for you to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Weber's Aufforderung zum Tanz is an asking of a partner to dance, as 'Come Dancing' is.

clue.text: Walton's to lose distinction when account is kept

definitions.note: the possessive points to a work by William Walton, not the man

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the account abbreviation sits within the verb

parts.note: to fade is to become less distinct

explanation.surface: Walton is set to lose his distinction once his accounts are held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. Façade is William Walton's entertainment of poems by Edith Sitwell recited over music.
explanation.definitionFit: Façade is the title of William Walton's best-known early work, so it is Walton's.

clue.text: Facial treatment to save the RAF

definitions.note: a noun here: a facial is a cosmetic preparation or treatment for the face

indicators.note: treatment means the following words are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A face cream marketed as rescuing the Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facial treatment' reads as one phrase, but 'treatment' is the anagram signal on SAVE THE RAF; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a lotion applied to the face after shaving, a product for the face.

clue.text: Attractive aspect of fairly old England?

parts.note: getting on in years, aging, is what makes someone fairly old

explanation.surface: Asks whether the charm of the old country lies in its being somewhat dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming or pleasing, a close synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Talk quietly to conductor

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

explanation.surface: A word in private with the orchestra's conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the conductor is Simon Rattle, then of the Berlin Philharmonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is idle or childish talk, chatter.

clue.text: Desire to get understanding horizontally?

parts.note: to long is to desire
wise means having understanding

explanation.surface: Wanting to gain insight while lying flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link; the question mark admits that lengthwise is only loosely horizontal.
explanation.definitionFit: Longwise means along the length, lying lengthways as opposed to upright.

clue.text: One given 23 covers America with new stars

definitions.note: 23 is the second part of the Weber title, so this is someone devoted to that dance

indicators.note: covers means the rearranged word wraps around the abbreviation
new signals the word stars takes a fresh arrangement

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A composer devoted to the dance covers America with fresh stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'new' gives STRAS before 'covers' wraps it round. Johann Strauss was the waltz king.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss the younger, the waltz king, was famously devoted to that dance.

clue.text: Pod sadly deceases

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A pod mournfully passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed case is a pod or capsule that holds a plant's seeds.

clue.text: See next page — setter's after the French astronomer

indicators.note: after places the setter's piece behind the French article

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed to send a reader to the next page
le is French for the
the setter speaks of himself as me, so setter's is my

explanation.surface: A footnote sending you overleaf, with the setter chasing a French astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO (please turn over) is common in crosswords. Ptolemy was the Alexandrian astronomer of the earth-centred universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy of Alexandria was the great astronomer whose Almagest described an earth-centred cosmos.

clue.text: Pipe going a little way into the wine

indicators.note: into means the short unit goes inside the wine

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
an inch is a little way, abbreviated in

explanation.surface: A drop of liquid trickles a short distance into the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' is a link; IN is the abbreviation for inch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, a kind of musical pipe.

clue.text: Composer with king on island broadcasting

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: the lion is the king of beasts
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
R/T stands for radio telephony, transmitting by radio

explanation.surface: A composer and a king broadcasting on an island radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Lionel Bart wrote the musical Oliver!
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Bart was the British songwriter who composed the musical Oliver!

clue.text: Composer's written a lot of stuff keeping the left hand from the right

clue.text: Composer's weight in car going up

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in puts the weight inside the turned vehicle
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a tram is a tramcar
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a weight

explanation.surface: A composer's weight sits in a car on its way uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' gives MART, read upward in the down light, and 'in' places the weight inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is the classical Austrian composer.

clue.text: See 11
Composer's friendly address in Cardiff

definitions.meaning: Johann Sebastian ..., with 's as is linking the two definitions
in Wales '...' is an affectionate form of address, like dear

explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff is the Welsh capital; Welsh speakers call friends 'bach', meaning little or dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach is both the great German composer and Welsh for little, used as a term of endearment.

clue.text: See 21
Singer and golfer, about 6

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the golfer's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A singer and a golfer, around six of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link. The singer is Elvis Presley.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the singer known as the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Excavated girls inverted for remembrance

indicators.note: inverted here means turned end to end, its two halves trading places

parts.note: Ophelia says rosemary is for remembrance in Hamlet

explanation.surface: Two girls whose names are swapped round as a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girls' hints that the herb splits into two girls' names, ROSE and MARY, which change places. The Mary Rose, Henry VIII's warship, was raised from the Solent in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mary Rose is the Tudor warship raised from the seabed in 1982, so famously excavated.
